title: Variation in negative and positive domestic coverage across media outlets

methods.selection: Publication country equals evaluated-government country. Fixed 71-country groups. Retain country-months with n>=30, then all their nonempty outlet-months without a further monthly threshold.
methods.point: One exact source domain, not a corporate parent or ownership family. Each domain belongs to one publication country in this extract.
methods.outlet_rate: Sum of sign counts across the outlet's eligible observed months / sum of all its articles over those same months. A pooled period share, not a mean of monthly rates. Zero labels remain in the denominator.
methods.main_distribution: Equal weight per outlet. Boxplot and summary mean/SD describe the outlet distribution; they do not reproduce equal-country monthly group means in figures16/19.
methods.within_country: Calculate sample SD (ddof=1) of the pooled outlet rates within each country; countries with fewer than two outlets have undefined SD and are excluded from this plot. Each retained country has equal weight in the supplement.
methods.small_samples: Retain all outlets in both figures. Gray open dots identify outlet total n<30, or countries containing such an outlet. CSVs separately report calculations after removing outlets with total n<30; this is a sensitivity check, not a change to the main sample.
methods.statistics: Sample SD uses ddof=1; quartiles use linear interpolation; IQR=Q3-Q1. All numerical CSV rates and SDs use 0-to-1 units; multiply by100 for percentages or percentage points.
methods.boxplot: Box=Q1 toQ3; line=median; whiskers=endmost observations within1.5IQR; diamond=mean; all observations shown as country/domain-stable jittered dots.
methods.labels: Low/Middle/High are relative groups based on each country's mean2022–2025 V-Dem v2x_freexp_altinf, with fixed24/23/24countries. They are not absolute classifications of media freedom.

limitations: Between-outlet dispersion pooled within a freedom group combines within-country and between-country differences; the supplement isolates variation among the observed outlets within each country.
Outlets do not necessarily cover the same months or events; pooled rates reflect their observed time and story mix.
Small samples can create extreme rates. Source domains, genre inclusion and collection gaps are not audited here.
Higher dispersion does not mechanically cause a higher mean; a few high-rate outlets can raise both. Negative coverage alone does not establish media bias.
No population inference, uncertainty intervals, audience weights, temporal-volatility estimates or causal effects are claimed.
